apiEndpoints.summary: Every auction for operators (latest first, optionally by status): video, creator, price, bids, timing, outcome.
Cancels an auction that is open or awaiting its decision, with a recorded reason; the leading bid is released.
Creator accounts with their verification state; `?verified=false` lists the review queue.
Records the outcome of a creator's 18 U.S.C. § 2257 review.
A creator's 2257 document (`?ref=private/documents/<uuid>.<ext>`), for operators only; never cached.
Operator overview: money, catalogue and the three queues that need a human.
Payout requests with their creator; `?status=` filters.
Advances a payout.
The platform for operators: environment, database (size, rows per table), migration history, whether a reset is allowed.
The database backups kept in private storage, newest first.
Backs the whole database up now (gzipped JSON of every table, in private storage).
Deletes a backup from private storage.
Downloads a backup file (`?download=1`), or describes it: tables, rows, migrations.

Factory reset: backs the database up first (unless asked not to), wipes it and rebuilds it from the migrations — development deployments only (OROCHIA_ALLOW_DATABASE_RESET, never the indexed production), after the operator typed “reset <database>”. The operator and the owner are kept.
Content reports, newest first; `?status=` filters.
Moves a report through triage (open → in review → resolved).
Every account (filter by `?role=`, `?suspended=`, `?q=`): role, verification and suspension state.
Suspends an account (it can no longer sign in, and its open sessions are refused on their next request; its open auctions are cancelled and their bids released), reinstates it, or changes its role.
The catalogue for moderation: every video with its creator, state and open reports; `?state=removed` lists takedowns.
Takes a video down (DMCA, terms, a confirmed report) with a recorded reason — cancelling its auction — or restores it.
Lists auctions by tab: open, upcoming, ended (sold), bidding (yours) or selling (your own).
Puts one of the creator's ready videos up for auction (start, end, starting price, rights, how it ends).
The creator cancels their auction while nobody has bid; the video gets its previous visibility back.
An auction as the viewer sees it: price, minimum next bid, timing, recent bids (aliases), and their own standing.
Places a bid in Orochia credits; they are held while the bid leads and released when it is outbid.
The creator accepts the best bid (the video is sold to its bidder) or declines it (the credits go back).
Server-Sent Events of an auction: each bid (amount, alias, new end) and every change of state.
E-mails a password-reset link (1 h) to the address, if an active account uses it.
Password login — a session cookie for the browser, a bearer token for a native app.
The signed-in account (with whether its e-mail is verified), or `user: null`.
The provider's redirect: checks the state, exchanges the code, then signs in (linked account or same verified address) or sends a new person to complete their account.
Sends the browser to the provider's consent page (state + PKCE kept in a signed 10-minute cookie).
Creates the account of a new Google / Facebook sign-in after the person gives a date of birth (18+), certifies it and accepts the terms.
The provider sign-in waiting to become an account: what the completion form can prefill.
The sign-in providers this deployment offers (only those whose keys are configured).
Creates an account (a member — creators are opened later, never an administrator), signs it in and e-mails the link that verifies its address — until then the account can do nothing else.
E-mails a new verification link to the signed-in account (the previous link stops working).
Sets a new password with the link's one-time token (1 h).
Whether a username is free (unique address orochia.com/@username), with a free one suggested when it is not.
Verifies an e-mail address with the link's one-time token (48 h); refreshes the session of that account.
Catalogue statistics for administrators, from the database.
Lists challenges by tab: open, calls (open calls), done (delivered), inbox (yours to answer or deliver), mine, backing.

Opens a challenge: a creator's goal (pledges until the deadline, all or nothing), a request to one creator (the sender's offer is held at once; the creator has three days to answer) or an open call for any creator (the author's pot is held; creators apply and the author picks one).
A challenge as the viewer sees it: progress, deadlines, backers (aliases), applications and what the viewer may do.
The creator a request was sent to accepts it (and must deliver in time) or declines it (every pledge comes back).
A verified creator applies to take an open call, with a short note for its author.
The author of an open call picks one applicant, who now has the delivery window to make it.
The author withdraws an open challenge (a goal, a request not answered yet, an open call): every pledge comes back.
What the creator can deliver: their ready videos not used elsewhere, or the stories posted since they committed.
The creator delivers a video or a story: the backers' pledges are paid and they can watch it.
Pledges Orochia credits to an open challenge; they are held until it is delivered and come back if it is not.
A goal's creator starts it as soon as the goal is reached (pledging stops; the delivery window begins).
Server-Sent Events of a challenge: each pledge (amount, alias, new total) and every change of state.
Sends a contact request (accepted at once when the other person already asked).
Removes a contact or withdraws a request (either side).
Accepts or rejects a request addressed to you, or blocks the other person.
Lists the signed-in user's active direct conversations.
Starts or retrieves a conversation with a specified user.
Lists messages in a conversation and marks unread messages as read.
Sends a direct message in a conversation.
Realtime Server-Sent Events (SSE) stream for instant direct messages and notifications.
Your earnings for a period (?period=30d|90d|12m|all): totals, views, each video's revenue, the trend, payments and payouts.
Downloads your earnings as CSV (?kind=transactions|videos&period=…), for your accounting.
The signed-in creator's balance, lifetime earnings and payout history — from the ledger.
Requests a payout to your saved payout account (an encrypted snapshot is kept); balance checked and reserved atomically.
A creator's public page: profile, videos, the collections you may open and, signed in, how you relate to them.
Unfollows a creator.
Follows a creator; the follow stays PENDING until the creator approves it.
The public feed and the explore search (`?q=`, `?tag=`, paginated); with the featured creator and popular tags.
Content reports.
Opens a creator space for a member: the account becomes CREATOR, pending its 18 U.S.C. § 2257 review (uploads open once an operator verifies it).
Records your date of birth (18+) when the account has none yet; once set it cannot be changed here.
Lists the accounts blocked by the signed-in user.
Your editor drafts (newest first), with a short-lived link to each original clip; expired ones are removed.
Keeps an edit as a draft: records its settings and returns a Tus session to send the original clip straight to Bunny.
Deletes one of your drafts with its clip and music.
One of your drafts, with a short-lived link to its original clip.
Saves new edit settings or form values on a draft (the clip is not sent again); it is kept longer.
Removes the music track of a draft.
The music track of one of your drafts (private: served to you only).
Keeps (or replaces) the music track of a draft — MP3, M4A, AAC, WAV or OGG up to 25 MB.
Tells that a draft's original clip is fully sent, so it can be opened again before Bunny finishes processing.
A creator approves a follower (opening followers-only videos to them) or removes them.
Lists the external OAuth providers linked to the signed-in account.
Unlinks a connected OAuth provider identity from the signed-in account.
Lists invitations sent by the signed-in user.
Sends an invitation to join Orochia to a friend or collaborator.
Your reusable audience lists (private to you), with their size.
Creates an audience list (names are unique per account).
Deletes one of your lists; the videos and collections it opened close to its members.
Renames one of your lists.
Removes someone from one of your lists (`?userId=`): what the list opened closes to them.
The people in one of your lists.
Adds an account to one of your lists by username (idempotent; the list stays private).
Your followers, the creators you follow, your contacts and pending requests.
Your notifications, newest first, 25 at a time (`before` = an ISO date to page back), with the unread count.
Marks notifications read: the ones listed, or all of them.
Where your earnings are sent — shown masked (e.g.
Saves (or replaces) where your earnings are sent; the details are checked and encrypted at rest.
Reads the signed-in user's own profile and settings (private fields included: e-mail, date of birth).
Updates the signed-in user's own profile and preferences (only the fields sent).
Your stories of the last 30 days — up, encoding or expired — with their figures.
Your Orochia credits: balance (and what is held behind your leading bids and challenge pledges), the packs you can buy, how you can pay for them, and your history.
Buys credits: returns the gateway's hosted checkout (card, Apple Pay, Google Pay — card details never reach Orochia); the gateway's signed webhook adds the credits.
Prometheus metrics, behind a bearer token (METRICS_AUTH_TOKEN).
The ways a buyer can pay on this deployment: credits (the wallet), then the external gateways.
Platform revenue, computed from the ledger only (administrators).
Your playlists, most recently changed first.
Creates a playlist.
Deletes a playlist (owner only).
A collection and its videos, for a viewer its permission admits (others get a 404).
Renames a collection, edits its description or who may open it (owner only).
Removes a video from a playlist (owner only).
Adds a video at the end of a playlist (owner only, idempotent).
Collections other accounts invited you to.
Reference content classifications and age ratings (Kids Safe, General, Teens, Mature, Adult).
Default avatar and banner presets users can choose without uploading custom files.
The stories rail: one ring per creator with current stories you may see (yours first, then unseen), signed for you.
Publishes an image story (24 h) from an image stored by /api/uploads (category "stories"); verified creators only.
Withdraws a story: its creator or an operator.
Removes your like (idempotent).
Likes a story you may see (idempotent).
Counts a view of a story you may see — once per viewer, never the creator's own.
Starts a video story: records it and returns a Tus session straight to Bunny (stories collection).

apiEndpoints.access: session · role depends on the request
apiEndpoints.summary: Stores an avatar or a profile banner (any account), a thumbnail, a story image or a 2257 document (creators); size and type checked per kind.
Unblocks a previously blocked user.
Blocks or unblocks a user: toggles block state on POST.
The creator deletes their video (refused while it is in an auction, and for a video its challenge's backers paid for).
The creator edits their video (an auctioned or challenge video keeps its audience): title, description, visibility, unlock price, tags, comments open.
The auction a video is in (open, awaiting its decision or sold), as the viewer sees it; null when there is none.
The comments of a video you may watch, oldest first; removed ones keep their place without text.
Comments on a video you may watch, or replies to one of its comments.
Removes a comment: its author, the video's creator or an operator.
A video's public metadata and figures (and whether you liked it); the stream is only served by /stream.
A five-minute signed link to the video's MP4 file, for its author and for a buyer whose grant includes downloading.
Removes your like (idempotent).
Likes a video you may watch (idempotent).
Counts a share of a video you may watch; the shared link still enforces the video's access.
Authorises a viewer and returns a short-lived signed HLS URL (AGENTS.md §2.A).
Starts the purchase of a video unlock.
Bunny Stream encoding events (https://bunny.net/docs/stream/webhooks), signed v1 with the library's Read-Only API key (BUNNY_WEBHOOK_SECRET).
Gateway payment notifications.
